key_insight: Cyclically driven metallic glass obeys a single dynamic scaling framework that links sub-yield aging and over-yield rejuvenation through different energy-injection pathways: macroscopic plastic work above yield and localized elastic stress fluctuations below yield.
engineering_relevance: This provides a predictive route to tune amorphous-material stability, relaxation, and rejuvenation under cyclic loading by controlling strain amplitude and loading rate.
method: Molecular dynamics simulations of a metallic glass under cyclic deformation
Analyze energy landscape evolution across sub-yield and over-yield regimes
Compare macroscopic plastic work scaling with localized stress-fluctuation scaling
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a unified scaling law and an exact identity connecting the relaxation attenuation exponent to the stress-fluctuation exponent, supporting the proposed common mechanism.
watch_item: The framework is simulation-based, so experimental validation across compositions, temperatures, and loading protocols will be needed before broad application.
paper_title: Universal Dynamic Scaling for Sub-Yield Aging and Over-Yield Rejuvenation in A Cyclically Driven Metallic Glass
